quick.summary: How to turn a simple observation into a deep insight about user behavior.
quick.takeaway: Find out how they view the world. Design to match their mental model.

parts.title: Find their mental model

beats.line: People keep ignoring our helpful sorting tool. Why do they scroll forever?
Think of a person organizing clothes in a large closet.
Some people hang them by color, others by season.
Exactly. Those are completely different ways of seeing the world.
They expect the closet to match their own logic.
In research, we call this their cognitive schema.
Can I just say their mental model?
Yes. Their mental model is what matters.
They scroll because your sorting does not match how they think.
So how do I figure out what their model actually is?

parts.cliff: Learn how to build a model in part two.

beats.line: You find their model by listening to the exact words they use.
Like when they call a folder a bucket instead?
Yes. Or when they group things that seem unrelated.
The raw finding is just how they sort items.
So if they group shoes by price, money is their focus.
Exactly. The insight is that they are worried about spending.
And we should design the tool to ease that worry.
Now you are translating a fact into a human insight.
I will change our labels to match their bucket idea.
You are thinking exactly like the user now.

quiz.question: What does a mental model represent in design?
options: How the user naturally thinks about and organizes the world.
The exact visual layout of a screen.
A map of all the technical database fields.
The brand guidelines your team must follow.
quiz.explanation: A mental model is the internal logic a person uses to understand how something should work.

quiz.question: A raw finding is exactly the same thing as a human insight.
quiz.explanation: A raw finding is what happened. An insight explains the deeper human worry or motivation behind it.
